boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Stony Lake record (July 28, 1863) in Operations Against the Sioux in North Dakota [July 1863]. The march to the Missouri and the July 29-30 skirmishes at the river are context. Campaign-wide marches, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field names the District of Minnesota and the Santee and Teton Sioux without figures; the live field reads 0. Sibley estimates the warriors at no less than 2,200 to 2,500 and, from scouts' and prisoners' information, the combined camp at nearly 10,000 souls. Crooks gives at least 2,000 mounted men.
claims.rationale: Opponents' estimates of the attacking force on July 28 (2,200 to 2,500; at least 2,000) and of the whole combined camp (10,000 souls, undated, from scouts' and prisoners' information), of different scopes. No account by the Dakota bands was inspected; their numbers, aims and losses come from their opponents' estimates, prisoners' or scouts' statements relayed by them, or the NPS summary. None is adopted as a matched opening strength.

claims.value: The frozen US commander is Brigadier General Henry Hastings Sibley. The frozen and live Native American commander is Inkpaduta (no rank; the live page tags him [CS], not adopted); none of the inspected reports names him, so his role is not established here. Sibley says the regiments took their positions before his orders reached them and that he formed the column in line of battle and resumed the march; Crooks credits Averill's deployment.
claims.rationale: Command roles from interested reports; no automatic sole credit.

open_questions: Baker's report (the Tenth led the column that morning), Marshall's report, the Dakota account and maps remain deferred. No targeted follow-up was used for this record.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Sibley's August 7, 1863 report covers all three July engagements and is an interested account; Crooks's August 5 report (Sixth Minnesota) also covers all three and is a separate family. Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.

No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting. Participants are named as the sources name them; characterizations in the sources (including 'hostile', 'savages', 'massacre' or 'battle') are quoted as the sources' own words and not adopted.
